patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition and personality change in a 53-year-old restaurant manager, with family history of early dementia.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. M. is a 53-year-old right-handed Hispanic man referred by his wife for progressive personality and behavioral changes over 2 years. She describes him as formerly highly motivated, organized, and ambitious. Two years ago, his behavior changed dramatically at work: he began making offensive comments to staff and customers, misappropriated cash from the register (which he denied), and was terminated after a customer altercation. At home, he has become increasingly impulsive — making large unauthorized purchases, getting into fights with neighbors, and ignoring personal hygiene. He eats voraciously, consuming all food in the refrigerator repeatedly. He insists on watching only boxing matches on television and becomes combative when interrupted. His alcohol consumption has escalated from occasional social use to 8-10 beers daily. He has no insight into any of these changes and reports feeling 'fine.' Family history is notable for his father, who had behavioral changes and dementia in his early 60s. Neurological review of systems negative.

results.title: Predictive genetic testing in C9orf72
results.finding: Predictive testing for C9orf72 in minors is controversial; most guidelines recommend deferring until adulthood with genetic counseling; son should be informed of risk

output.summary: Predictive genetic testing for adult-onset neurodegenerative conditions (including C9orf72 repeat expansion) in minors is generally deferred until adulthood per major genetic counseling society guidelines, given that the test result cannot yet modify clinical management and autonomy considerations are paramount. First-degree relatives of C9orf72 expansion carriers have a 50% risk of carrying the mutation. Published guidelines recommend that predictive testing in adults be preceded by genetic counseling. Clinical correlation recommended.
